key_insight: A closed-loop validation-repair system greatly improved clinical LLM outputs from imperfect schema compliance to near-perfect interoperability readiness.
clinical_relevance: For healthcare systems that need ICD-10, CPT, or FHIR-compatible outputs, this approach could reduce structured-data errors before integration into electronic health records.
method: Tested Qwen2.5 7B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Gemma2 9B locally
Evaluated 320 clinical scenarios across 10 specialties, for 960 model-scenario pairs
Compared baseline outputs with a validation-repair loop for schema compliance
evidence_signal: Baseline compliance ranged from 85.9% to 91.6%, while validation-repair raised overall compliance to 99.0% with 98.4% to 99.4% across models; McNemar p-values were below 0.001.
watch_item: High schema compliance does not guarantee clinical correctness, and deployment still needs careful validation of downstream coding and exchange workflows.
paper_title: Closed-Loop Validation-Repair for Healthcare Interoperability: A Multi-Model Study of Schema Compliance in Clinical LLMs
